summary: Primary context assembly, memory persistence, the quality/hardening bundle, cross-org isolation of multiplayer context, and — for a clone — the regression verdict against the deployment it replicates.
not_covered: Model quality: these checks prove what reaches the model, not what the model then says.
Live cross-org traffic — test:org-isolation measures a database, the functional lane's rls rows measure the deployed one.

The mold's own tests here (cwd `default_profile`) run on the DEFAULT deployment profile, since they pin its words and fields; this app's own profile is graded by the `vocabulary` row (what its model reads), not by them.

checks.name: test:prompt-context
checks.why: Primary context is the corpus the agent answers from; the wrong assembly is a wrong answer with a confident tone.

checks.name: test:memory
checks.why: Memory persistence is what makes the second conversation cheaper than the first.

checks.name: test:qm-hardening
checks.why: The mold's own hardening bundle over context, memory, browser security, leases, step context, sign-in, gates and chat.

checks.name: vocabulary
checks.why: The rows above run the mold's own tests on the DEFAULT profile, because they pin its words; this row grades THIS app's. For each of its packs, the mold's agent-vocabulary gate in pack mode (npm run check:agent-vocabulary -- --pack packs/<id> --allow <its vocabulary-allow.json>) renders everything the model reads under the pack's own profile — prompts, briefing, every tool's name and parameters, every subagent, real offline tool results — and fails on any base word (customer, deployment, implementation, rollout, FDE) left in it; an app without packs is graded on the default surface. A leak here is an agent reasoning in the base product's words about this app's records.

stdout: vocabulary (pack [a-z0-9-]+|default profile \(no packs\)): pass|vocabulary: not measured

skip_on.else: This mold has no agent-vocabulary gate (npm run check:agent-vocabulary), so nothing measured what the model reads in this app's words. Refresh the mold from source per {mold}/MOLD.md, then re-run: python3 .claude/scripts/lanes.py {app_id} --lane context

checks.name: test:org-isolation
checks.why: Multiplayer context is shared processes across one workspace; a leak here hands one customer another customer's work. Runs AS the deployed application: the runner places the app's own DATABASE_URL (app_rw) in the environment by name. Invoked directly rather than through `npm run test:org-isolation`: that script hardcodes Node's --env-file=.env.local, which aborts with exit 9 before the test starts whenever the file is absent, although the test itself reads DATABASE_URL from the environment first (measured 2026-09-13: the first run of this check ended at `node: .env.local: not found`).

requires.else: Needs this app's own DATABASE_URL (the app_rw role) in the environment — as postgres the check cannot detect a leak at all, because postgres has BYPASSRLS. The runner reads it by name from the app's secret store once the app is deployed (provision.py <app_id> --deploy; a vm app: --verify-db). The value is never printed.

checks.name: clone.regression
checks.why: This app claims to replicate a live deployment. The diff clone.py measured is the context verdict; without this row the lane would overwrite it with a greener answer than the evidence supports.

requires.else: Only a clone has a live deployment to diff against; this app was not stamped with clone_of.
